The four product releases in the interval (v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.3.1, v0.3.2) each record a dated observation report with an artifact-verified note, and the semver-v1 release bindings carry those tag/commit mappings without erasing earlier ones. The one divergence found: `harness.name` still reads `pi coding agent` while the interval's later work and this session ran under a different harness. findings.resolved: The `release` finding that blocked this repository since 2026-10-07 is cleared by the alpha.20 `release_history: recoverable-v1` profile, which anchors the boundary at its establishment rather than demanding every published value match the current one. Root cause was this repository's own bookkeeping — recording a release observation had re-pointed effective_commit at that release's commit — and that is retained in .yolo/reports/upgrade-alpha16-proposal.json and issue #116 rather than being rewritten away. The two v0.3.2 entries that had recorded an annotated tag object instead of a commit were corrected to the same immutable commit 75cfffb, preserving the references.

findings.detail: Acceptance was actually run at this revision rather than inherited. npm test passes 221 tests across 18 files; npx tsc --noEmit is clean; npm run build succeeds; and npm run e2e passes 70 with 1 skipped against the deterministic stubbed client, writing no repository records. The committed build output was checked against a fresh build of the same source: after normalising the one embedded build-id string the bundles are byte-identical, so the committed `dist/client/` is faithful to source. That build id reads 8a9be5e while HEAD is 9680736, which is the documented ordering (ARCHITECTURE.md records that both build-ID files carry the built source revision and that the tagged source follows an assets-only commit) rather than staleness. Two honest limits are retained. First, the e2e/review capture set is not byte-reproducible across sessions: this run changed 21 of 79 tracked images, and the determinism guard in e2e/determinism.spec.ts compares two captures within one session, which passes, so the churn is cross-session only and remains an open gap rather than a regression. Second, the recorded live gaps in docs/verification.md — first-login, missing-gh, browser-open, multi-page pagination and mid-session auth loss — remain unobserved live, except the auth-loss path which is now forced read-only in the live E2E. No delivery claim is made beyond what the four release observation reports record, and each names the command actually run.

checkpoint_outcome.reason: A successful report is necessary but not sufficient. The validator walks the whole published chain and requires every report in it to name ownership, congruence, verification and continuity, byte-identical to committed content. Five reports in the chain predate that discipline: onboarding-l1-proposal.json, activation-2026-10-05.json, delivery-2026-10-05-5.json, delivery-2026-10-05-22.json and delivery-2026-10-06-alpha13.json name no congruence finding, and delivery-2026-10-06-final.json names neither congruence nor continuity. The finding it raises is "Report omits a required semantic rule".
checkpoint_outcome.why_not_repairable_here: Those reports are published, committed evidence. The same validator refuses to read any report that differs from its committed bytes ("Checkpoint evidence is not unchanged committed content"), so the missing findings cannot be added without rewriting published history. Both routes are prohibited: the protocol forbids clearing a checkpoint to make a check succeed and requires failed findings to be retained with cited resolutions.
checkpoint_outcome.probe: Tested in a disposable clone rather than assumed. Adding the two missing rules to delivery-2026-10-06-final.json changed the error from "Report omits a required semantic rule" to "Checkpoint evidence is not unchanged committed content", proving both halves of the diagnosis: the obligation is genuinely missing, and the repair is genuinely forbidden. The clone was deleted; this repository was not modified by the probe.
checkpoint_outcome.rule_history: The four-obligation requirement is not new. The adopted protocol stated it from the first adoption commit fa6ec88 (2026-10-05), in the reports section and at Q3. The 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-06 reports were published without it, so this is a latent nonconformity in this repository's own record, not a rule change arriving after the fact.
checkpoint_outcome.classification: This is a target record defect with a historical cause, not an upstream rule defect: the rule was satisfiable at every point when those reports were written. Unlike the release finding (upstream yolo-dev#73, rule assumed a value could never legitimately change) this one has a local remedy that respects history - a forward-citing report that carries the missing obligations forward, if the validator is ever taught to accept obligation coverage inherited across the chain rather than demanded per report.
checkpoint_outcome.what_this_report_does_achieve: It is a complete, cited, successful review of the 75-commit interval under the current pin, and it is retained as the evidence for that interval. It is deliberately NOT recorded as the checkpoint, because doing so would assert a passing chain that does not exist.
checkpoint_outcome.next_action_owner: Maintainer decision: either accept that the checkpoint stays at 31c0f8b until the chain rule is addressed upstream, or authorize an explicit, recorded exception. The agent will not rewrite published reports or weaken the rule to clear its own finding.
